passages.text: So I made up my mind not to make another painful visit to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul made a decision.
Paul decided not to visit the Corinthians again in pain.
Paul did not want to make another painful visit to them.
passages.original: Ἔκρινα γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ τοῦτο τὸ μὴ πάλιν ἐν λύπῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν

passages.text: For if I grieve you, who is left to cheer me but those whom I have grieved?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle and a leader in the church.
Paul sometimes needs to correct the believers in Corinth.
Paul says, "If I cause you sorrow, then you will feel pain."
If you feel pain because of me, you cannot make me happy.
Only those I have made sad can bring me comfort.
If I grieve you, then no one else can cheer me except you.
You are the ones I have grieved.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ λυπῶ ὑμᾶς καὶ τίς ὁ εὐφραίνων με εἰ μὴ ὁ λυπούμενος ἐξ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: I wrote as I did so that on my arrival I would not be saddened by those who ought to make me rejoice. I had confidence in all of you, that you would share my joy.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul wrote this letter to the Corinthians.
Paul wanted to avoid sadness when he visited them.
Paul did not want to be saddened by the Corinthians.
The Corinthians should have brought Paul joy.
Paul trusted all the Corinthians.
Paul believed the Corinthians would share his joy.
passages.original: καὶ ἔγραψα τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἵνα μὴ ἐλθὼν λύπην σχῶ ἀφ’ ὧν ἔδει με χαίρειν πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ πάντας ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἡ ἐμὴ χαρὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐστιν

passages.text: For through many tears I wrote you out of great distress and anguish of heart, not to grieve you but to let you know how much I love you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul wrote to the Corinthians.
Paul felt great distress.
Paul’s heart was full of anguish.
Paul cried many tears.
Paul wrote his letter during this pain.
Paul did not want to make the Corinthians sad.
Paul wanted them to know his love.
Paul’s love for them was very great.
passages.original: ἐκ γὰρ πολλῆς θλίψεως καὶ συνοχῆς καρδίας ἔγραψα ὑμῖν διὰ πολλῶν δακρύων οὐχ ἵνα λυπηθῆτε ἀλλὰ τὴν ἀγάπην ἵνα γνῶτε ἣν ἔχω περισσοτέρως εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Now if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but all of you—to some degree, not to overstate it.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul addresses the church in Corinth.
If anyone has caused grief,
that person has not mainly grieved me, Paul.
Instead, that person has grieved all of you, the church.
This grief affects you to some degree.
I do not want to exaggerate the matter.
passages.original: Εἰ δέ τις λελύπηκεν οὐκ ἐμὲ λελύπηκεν ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ μέρους ἵνα μὴ ἐπιβαρῶ πάντας ὑμᾶς

passages.text: The punishment imposed on him by the majority is sufficient for him.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul addressed a man who caused grief in the church.
Most of the church decided to punish this man.
This punishment is enough for him.
passages.original: ἱκανὸν τῷ τοιούτῳ ἡ ἐπιτιμία αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ τῶν πλειόνων

passages.text: So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Corinth.
A man in the church caused grief.
The church punished this man.
Now, you should do the opposite of punishing him.
You should forgive this man.
You should comfort him.
If you do not forgive and comfort him, he may be overwhelmed by too much sorrow.
passages.original: ὥστε τοὐναντίον μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς χαρίσασθαι καὶ παρακαλέσαι μή πως τῇ περισσοτέρᾳ λύπῃ καταποθῇ ὁ τοιοῦτος

passages.text: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul urges the believers in Corinth.
He tells them to reaffirm their love for the man who was punished.
Paul wants them to show love to him again.
passages.original: διὸ παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς κυρῶσαι εἰς αὐτὸν ἀγάπην

passages.text: My purpose in writing you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul wanted to test the church.
Paul wanted to see if the church would obey in every way.
Paul’s purpose was to know if they would stand the test.
Paul wrote for this reason.
passages.original: Εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ἔγραψα ἵνα γνῶ τὴν δοκιμὴν ὑμῶν εἰ εἰς πάντα ὑπήκοοί ἐστε

passages.text: If you forgive anyone, I also forgive him. And if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake, in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
If you forgive anyone, I also forgive that person.
If I have forgiven anything, I have done it for your sake.
I have forgiven in the presence of Christ.
I do this so that Satan will not outwit us.
We are not unaware of Satan’s schemes.
passages.original: ᾧ δέ τι χαρίζεσθε κἀγώ καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ὃ κεχάρισμαι εἴ τι κεχάρισμαι δι’ ὑμᾶς ἐν προσώπῳ Χριστοῦ ἵνα μὴ πλεονεκτηθῶμεν ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ οὐ γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὰ νοήματα ἀγνοοῦμεν

passages.text: Now when I went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ and a door stood open for me in the Lord, I had no peace in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul went to Troas.
Paul went to preach the gospel of Christ.
The Lord opened a door for Paul in Troas.
Paul did not find his brother Titus in Troas.
Paul had no peace in his spirit because Titus was not there.
Paul said goodbye to the people in Troas.
Paul left Troas and went to Macedonia.
passages.original: Ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θύρας μοι ἀνεῳγμένης ἐν Κυρίῳ οὐκ ἔσχηκα ἄνεσιν τῷ πνεύματί μου τῷ μὴ εὑρεῖν με Τίτον τὸν ἀδελφόν μου ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἐξῆλθον εἰς Μακεδονίαν

passages.text: But thanks be to God, who always leads us triumphantly as captives in Christ and through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him.
passages.sermon:
God leads us.
God leads us in Christ.
God always leads us in triumph.
God makes us captives in Christ.
God uses us to spread the knowledge of Christ.
God spreads the knowledge of Christ everywhere through us.
The knowledge of Christ is like a fragrance.
We thank God for this.
passages.original: Τῷ δὲ Θεῷ χάρις τῷ πάντοτε θριαμβεύοντι ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τὴν ὀσμὴν τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ φανεροῦντι δι’ ἡμῶν ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ

passages.text: For we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are perishing.
passages.sermon:
We belong to Christ.
God sees us as the sweet aroma of Christ.
We are this aroma among people who are being saved.
We are also this aroma among people who are perishing.
passages.original: ὅτι Χριστοῦ εὐωδία ἐσμὲν τῷ Θεῷ ἐν τοῖς σωζομένοις καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις

passages.text: To the one, we are an odor of death and demise; to the other, a fragrance that brings life. And who is qualified for such a task?
passages.sermon:
We are the aroma of Christ to God.
Some people are being saved.
Some people are perishing.
To those who are perishing, we are a smell that comes from death and leads to death.
To those who are being saved, we are a fragrance that comes from life and leads to life.
Who is able to do such things?
passages.original: οἷς μὲν ὀσμὴ ἐκ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον οἷς δὲ ὀσμὴ ἐκ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν καὶ πρὸς ταῦτα τίς ἱκανός

passages.text: For we are not like so many others, who peddle the word of God for profit. On the contrary, in Christ we speak before God with sincerity, as men sent from God.
passages.sermon:
We are not like many people.
Many people peddle the word of God for profit.
We do not do this.
We speak in Christ.
We speak before God.
We speak with sincerity.
We speak as people sent from God.
passages.original: Οὐ γάρ ἐσμεν ὡς οἱ πολλοὶ καπηλεύοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐξ εἰλικρινείας ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐκ Θεοῦ κατέναντι Θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλοῦμεν
